title: The Dread of Begging
note: This is fear of the begging that costs you your honour.

couplets.plain: Even from those as dear as your eyes, who give gladly and hide nothing, not begging is worth ten million times more.
couplets.pm: Even from those as dear as your eyes, who hide nothing and give with joy that you have come, staying poor and not begging is ten million times better than growing rich by begging. Begging from such people only keeps your honour from being lost and adds nothing to it. Better to stay alive by hard effort.
couplets.sensitive: ranks those who beg far below those who don't

links.quote: not begging is worth ten million times more

couplets.plain: If the one who made the world wanted people to live even by begging, let him wander far and perish.
couplets.pm: If the maker of this world ordained that people should live even by begging, and not by effort, let that cruel one wander everywhere and perish as they do. On the day life enters the womb he sets, by past karma, its span, its food and the work that earns it. If he set begging as the work of some, he should suffer for that sin.

links.quote: let him wander far and perish
links.reason: Curses the maker of the world to say no one should have to beg to live: the target is the injustice.

couplets.plain: Nothing is harder than the hardness that says, “I will end the misery of poverty by begging.”
couplets.pm: Nothing is harder than the hardness of thinking you will end the pain of poverty by begging and not by effort. Effort is the right road and begging is not, so this is hardness, the stubbornness of acting without thought. Begging isn’t the way to end poverty.
couplets.sensitive: calls the decision to beg the hardest of hearts

links.quote: I will end the misery of poverty by begging
links.reason: No hardness is worse than planning to beg your way out of poverty.

couplets.plain: Even with no means left, the worth that won’t consent to beg is too great for all the space there is to hold.
couplets.pm: The calm that won’t agree to go and beg from others, even in poverty with nothing to enjoy, has a greatness that all the worlds together couldn’t hold. Worth rules out begging, so the refusal is credited to worth. People of worth don’t take that wrong road.
couplets.sensitive: praises refusing help even when destitute

links.quote: the worth that won’t consent to beg
links.reason: Having nothing at all still can’t make this worth beg, and all the space there is can’t hold it.

couplets.plain: Even if it is gruel as thin as water, nothing is sweeter than eating what your own labour has brought.
couplets.pm: Even if what right effort has brought is cooked gruel as clear as water, nothing is sweeter than eating it. It has no thickness, but it didn’t come by shameful begging and it is your own, so it equals nectar. A little gained the right way gives great joy.

links.quote: what your own labour has brought
Even if it is gruel as thin as water

couplets.plain: Even if you beg water for a cow, there is nothing more shaming to the tongue than begging.
couplets.pm: A cow is dying of thirst and, thinking of righteousness, you beg someone to give it water. Even then nothing shames a tongue like that begging. Protecting cows is a great righteous act and water costs nothing, yet the shame of those words exceeds all others. Do righteousness by effort, not by begging.

links.quote: nothing more shaming to the tongue than begging
Even if you beg water for a cow

couplets.plain: I beg of everyone who begs: if you must beg, don’t beg from those who hide what they have.
couplets.pm: I am begging all who beg: if you must beg, don’t beg from those who hide what they have. “I beg” shows that begging isn’t needed, since the body won’t last even when fed by such a shameful act. This forbids the begging that costs you your honour.

links.quote: I beg of everyone who begs
don’t beg from those who hide what they have
links.reason: Direct advice for choosing whom to ask: stay away from those who hide what they have.

couplets.plain: The unsafe boat called begging will split apart when it strikes the rock called hiding.
couplets.pm: A man boards the unsafe boat called begging, thinking it will carry him across the sea of poverty. If on the way it strikes the hard ground of hiding, it splits apart. What should be crossed by effort he tries to cross by begging, and he never sees the far shore. So don’t board it.

links.reason: One meeting with hiding is enough to wreck it, so unsafe is this way of living.

links.quote: split apart when it strikes the rock called hiding
links.reason: Sends begging out as a boat and makes hiding the rock that splits it.

couplets.plain: The heart melts at the thought of begging. At the thought of hiding, even what is left dies.
couplets.pm: When I think how cruel it is for those with nothing to stand begging before those who have, my heart melts. When I think how cruel it is to see that and say “I have nothing,” even that melting heart perishes. Hiding is crueller than begging. Others all take it as the beggar’s heart that melts.

links.quote: The heart melts at the thought of begging
links.reason: Feels the beggar’s lot enough to melt the heart, and the hiding enough to kill it.

couplets.plain: At a mere word, the life goes out of those who beg. Where then does the life of those who hide go to hide?
couplets.pm: At the mere word “no” from those who hide what they have, life leaves the beggar. Yet those who speak it stay alive: where does theirs go to hide? Life leaving means standing helpless, moaning, “What shall we do now?” Words that kill the hearer should kill the speaker, but we don’t see that. Some make this the voice of one who fears to beg.

links.quote: At a mere word, the life goes out of those who beg
Where then does the life of those who hide go to hide?
